text.p: These are the leading stories in Zambia's newspapers on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and can not vouch for their accuracy.
- The government says it has no money to procure fertilisers for at least 660,000 peasant farmers under a credit scheme.
- The government will spend at least $720 million to improve the education system, the ministry of education said.

- The ruling Movement for Multiparty Democracy (MMD) said it would expel members who have been holding 'dark corner meetings' to identify a successor to president Frederick Chiluba when his second term, constitutionally his last, ends in 2001.
- Families of football players who died in a plane crash off the coast of Gabon have sued the state for negligence leading to the accident.
